text.p: Shareholders in Italian state-controlled telecoms holding Stet on Wednesday approved the introduction of a so-called golden share to be held by the Treasury in the future privatised group.

Stet chairman Guido Rossi told the extraordinary shareholders' meeting the use of the golden share was justified to avoid the risk the privatisation became just "a move from a public monopoly to a private monopoly."
The Stet sale is due to take place this autumn after the holding is merged with its fixed-line telephone unit Telecom Italia.
The golden share, to be introduced into the company's statutes on July 15, gives the Treasury special voting rights after it loses majority control for up to three years after the sell-off.
Italy has said it wants to create a stable core of shareholders in Stet when control passes into private hands.
The Treasury has already said that shareholders in Stet will be able to take a maximum three percent stake in the group after its privatisation.

It has also said the golden share could be dropped once the liberalisation of the domestic telecoms market reached a sufficiently advanced level and when a watchdog body set up to oversee the sector had consolidated its position.
However, legislation for the sale, including a bill to create the watchdog, has still not been approved by parliament.
